examples.japanese: {舞踏|ぶとう}{会|かい}に{招待|しょうたい}された。
examples.english: I was invited to a ball.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{舞踏|ぶとう}を{学|まな}んでいる。
{暗黒|あんこく}{舞踏|ぶとう}は{日本|にほん}{発祥|はっしょう}の{前衛的|ぜんえいてき}な{舞踊|ぶよう}{芸術|げいじゅつ}である。
examples.english: Butoh is an avant-garde dance art form that originated in Japan.

notes:
Refers to dance as a formal or artistic activity. Most commonly encountered in the compound {舞踏|ぶとう}{会|かい} (ball, dance party), and in {暗黒|あんこく}{舞踏|ぶとう} (butoh), a form of Japanese avant-garde dance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {舞踏|ぶとう}{会|かい}: ball, dance party
- {舞踏|ぶとう}{曲|きょく}: dance music
- {暗黒|あんこく}{舞踏|ぶとう}: butoh (avant-garde dance)
- {舞踏|ぶとう}{家|か}: dancer (professional)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {舞踊|ぶよう}: dance — broader term that includes both Japanese traditional dance and Western dance
- ダンス: dance — loanword for casual or modern dancing
- {踊|おど}り: dance — everyday word for dancing, especially folk or festival dances
- {舞|まい}: dance — refers specifically to the slow, elegant dance style of Noh and traditional court dance
